questions.question: What is an R-tree?

options.text: A balanced tree structure for indexing multi-dimensional spatial data using minimum bounding rectangles

questions.explanation: R-tree: spatial index for rectangles, polygons, points. Each node contains MBR (Minimum Bounding Rectangle) enclosing all children. Balanced: all leaves at same depth. Used in: PostGIS, SQLite, MongoDB.

questions.question: What is a Minimum Bounding Rectangle (MBR)?

options.text: The smallest axis-aligned rectangle that completely contains a spatial object or group of objects

questions.explanation: MBR: axis-aligned rectangle defined by (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y). Approximates complex shapes. R-tree nodes store MBRs of children. Enables fast overlap/containment tests.

questions.question: How does R-tree search work for a range query?

options.text: Start at root, only descend into children whose MBR intersects the query rectangle

questions.explanation: R-tree search: 1) Check if query rectangle intersects node's MBR. 2) If no intersection, skip entire subtree. 3) If intersects, recurse into children. 4) At leaves, check actual objects. Prunes non-overlapping branches.

questions.question: What is the key challenge when inserting into an R-tree?

options.text: Choosing which subtree to insert into to minimize MBR expansion and overlap

questions.explanation: Insert challenge: which child to choose? Goals: minimize MBR enlargement, minimize overlap between siblings. Overlap = multiple paths to search. Various heuristics: least enlargement, least overlap, combined.

questions.question: What happens when an R-tree node overflows?

options.text: The node splits into two nodes, distributing entries to minimize total MBR area and overlap

questions.explanation: Node split: when node exceeds capacity M. Split algorithms: linear (fast, simple), quadratic (better quality), R*-tree (best quality, reinserts). Goal: minimize dead space and overlap in resulting MBRs.

questions.question: What is the R*-tree improvement over basic R-tree?

options.text: Better split algorithm and forced reinsert strategy that improves tree structure

questions.explanation: R*-tree improvements: 1) Better split considering overlap, margin, area. 2) Forced reinsert: on overflow, reinsert 30% of entries instead of immediate split. Results in better-structured tree, faster queries.

questions.question: What is the typical node capacity (M) for an R-tree?

options.text: 50-100 entries, sized to fit a disk page

questions.explanation: Node capacity: typically sized to disk page (4KB-8KB). 50-100 entries common. Larger M = shallower tree, fewer disk reads. Trade-off: larger nodes = more entries to scan within node.

questions.question: R-tree vs Quadtree: when would you choose R-tree?

options.text: For indexing rectangles/polygons, handling non-uniform data distribution, and when you need guaranteed balance

questions.explanation: R-tree advantages: handles rectangles/polygons natively, self-balancing, better with clustered data. Quadtree: simpler, good for points, uniform distribution. R-tree: production spatial databases. Quadtree: games, simple apps.

questions.question: How does PostGIS use R-trees?

options.text: As the underlying index structure for GIST spatial indexes on geometry columns

questions.explanation: PostGIS: CREATE INDEX ON table USING GIST(geom). GIST uses R-tree internally. Enables fast: ST_Intersects, ST_Contains, ST_DWithin queries. Index stores MBRs, actual geometry checked only for candidates.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of R-tree search in the average case?

options.text: O(log n) for well-structured trees with minimal overlap

questions.explanation: R-tree search: O(log_M n) average case with good structure. Worst case: O(n) if all MBRs overlap (must check all paths). R*-tree minimizes overlap, keeping performance closer to O(log n).

questions.question: What is bulk loading in R-trees?

options.text: Building the tree from a sorted dataset all at once, producing better structure than repeated inserts

questions.explanation: Bulk loading: Sort-Tile-Recursive (STR) algorithm. Sort data, pack into nodes bottom-up. Results: minimal overlap, optimal packing, faster queries. Use when loading large static datasets.

questions.question: You're building a ride-sharing app that needs to find all drivers within a polygon (city boundary). Which index would you use?

options.text: R-tree spatial index to efficiently query drivers whose location intersects the polygon

questions.explanation: Polygon query: R-tree indexes driver locations. Query: find all points within polygon. R-tree first finds candidates via MBR intersection, then precise polygon containment check. Efficient for complex boundaries.
